classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the first compass bearing to obtain the angle at B, compare the two south-based directions, and use the resulting included angle in the area rule.

content.prompt:
Jane starts at point $A$. She walks 35 m on a bearing N30°E to point $B$. From $B$, she walks 50 m on a bearing S70°W to point $C$. She then returns directly to $A$, forming $\triangle ABC$.

Find the area of $\triangle ABC$, correct to one decimal place.

answer.short:
$562.4\text{ m}^2$

Reverse the first bearing to obtain the included angle $40^\circ$, then use the triangle area rule.
answer.worked:
From $B$, the bearing of $A$ is S30°W and the bearing of $C$ is S70°W.

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=70^\circ-30^\circ\\\angle ABC&=40^\circ\\A&=\frac12(35)(50)\sin40^\circ\\A&\approx562.4\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
